For the fallback implementation, it processes 1 byte at a time. For the haswell/westmere implementations, it processes more bytes at once.

The issue is that `handle_unicode_codepoint` reads 4 bytes at `*src_ptr + 2`. If the `\u` escape is at the very end of the string data (e.g., the string is `"\u` and the closing quote is missing), then `*src_ptr + 2` points to the byte right after `\u`, which is the last byte of the actual data. Reading `src[0]` through `src[3]` reads 4 bytes, which goes 3 bytes past the end of the actual data. With 32 bytes of padding, this should still be within bounds.

But wait - the crash is an UNKNOWN READ. Let me look at the specific scenario more carefully. The `parse_string` function processes the string and when it finds a backslash, it checks if the next char is `u`. If so, it calls `handle_unicode_codepoint`. The `src` pointer at that point points to the `\` character. So `*src_ptr + 2` points to the first hex digit after `\u`.

For the crash to happen, we need `*src_ptr + 2 + 3` (reading 4 bytes) to go past the end of the buffer including padding. That means `*src_ptr + 2 + 4 > length + 32`, i.e., `*src_ptr > length + 26`. But `*src_ptr` points to the `\` character which is within the string data, so `*src_ptr <= length - 1`. So `*src_ptr + 2 + 4 <= length + 5`, which is well within the 32-byte padding.

# entry point for oss-fuzz, so that fuzzers
# and build invocation can be changed without having
# to modify the oss-fuzz repo.
#
# invoke it from the git root.

# make sure to exit on problems
set -eux

for prog in zip cmake ninja; do
    if ! which $prog >/dev/null; then
        echo please install $prog
        exit 1
    fi
done


# build the corpus (all inputs are json, the same corpus can be used for everyone)
fuzz/build_corpus.sh

mkdir -p build
cd build

cmake .. \
-GNinja \
-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
-DSIMDJSON_BUILD_STATIC=On \
-DENABLE_FUZZING=On \
-DSIMDJSON_COMPETITION=Off \
-DSIMDJSON_FUZZ_LINKMAIN=Off \
-DSIMDJSON_GIT=Off \
-DSIMDJSON_GOOGLE_BENCHMARKS=Off \
-DSIMDJSON_DISABLE_DEPRECATED_API=On \
-DSIMDJSON_FUZZ_LDFLAGS=$LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE

cmake --build . --target all_fuzzers

cp fuzz/fuzz_* $OUT

# all fuzzers but one (the tiny target for utf8 validation) takes json
# as input, therefore use the same corpus of json files for all.
for f in $(ls $OUT/fuzz* |grep -v '.zip$') ; do
   cp ../corpus.zip $OUT/$(basename $f).zip
done
